newsitem.title: USA: Jury to decide punishment in trial of Texas mother.
newsitem.headline: Jury to decide punishment in trial of Texas mother.

text.p: Witnesses testified Monday that a Dallas woman convicted on one count of capital murder in the stabbing death of her two sons was an indifferent, at times abusive mother who gave drugs and liquor to her babysitter.

The testimony was part of the trial's punishment phase in which the jury that found Darlie Routier, 27, guilty in the June 6 deaths of her sons Devon, 6, and Damon, 5, must decide whether she gets the death penalty or a jail term.

Prosecutors said in the trial that Routier killed in a fit of rage about family financial difficulties and her ongoing weight problems. She had testified the children were murdered by a knife-wielding intruder who also attacked her while all three slept in their Rowlett, Texas home, near Dallas.

The jury Saturday found Routier guilty of capital murder in the death of her younger son, Damon. A second capital murder charge is pending in the death of Devon but prosecutors have not said if they will pursue it. Capital murder is a more serious charge than murder and carries with it the possibility of a death sentence.

Prosecutor Greg Davis told reporters after the verdict he would ask that Routier be put to death by lethal injection. "Anyone willing to take the life of two innocent children is willing to do anything," he said.
A Routier acquaintance, 18-year-old Allison Hennessey, testified Monday that Routier gave marijuana, liquor and cigarettes to a babysitter she and her husband Darin routinely used on weekends.
"She was an adult giving my best friend (the babysitter) things I dont agree with," Hennessey said. She and other witnesses also said the Routier boys often played outside without proper supervision.

A neighbour, Eileen Schirmer, told the jury she once saw Darlie Routier grab Devon by the back of his head and smash cake in his face when he sprayed water on her at his birthday party. "She said he was warned and got what he deserved," Schirmer said.
The defence, hoping to avoid the death sentence, was expected to put on witnesses later who would portray Routier as a loving mother.
A spokesman for the Texas Department of Corrections said Texas has six women on death row.

The last time a woman was executed in Texas was in 1863, when Chipita Rodriguez was hanged in San Patricio County in south Texas for killing a horse trader and stealing $600, the spokesman said. But at that time, and until 1923, executions were conducted by county governments, not the state.
All capital murder convictions are automatically appealed under Texas law.
